messages:
incident-bot: @sre-oncall PAGER: High error rate detected on /v1/generate in prod - threshold breached (5xx rate 8% over 5m). Auto-canary flagged. Please investigate. https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/1759456789

sre-oncall: acked. I'm on it. Quick summary: did we just push a deploy?

eng-release: pushed release/2026.05 to canary at 10:02 UTC (feature flag: new-metrics-write enabled for 10% of traffic). Included a DB migration: ALTER TABLE responses ADD COLUMN response_meta JSONB; migration uses an online migration helper. Canary showed failures after ~30s.

prod-support: seeing errors from customers: a few write requests 500'ing, some timeouts. Matt, can you quantify?

matt-support: quick stats from logs: 2.1% of total requests returning 500; 5 customers show elevated error rates (customers: acme-inc, polaris-ml, skyfarm). Error payloads: "ERROR: column \"response_meta\" does not exist" and occasional lock-timeout on write queries.

eng-release: hmm that message implies code expecting new column but migration hadn't completed on all DB pods. Canary nodes hit the new code path because flag rollout allowed writes. The migration job stuck at step 3 (backfill) due to long-running VACUUM/LOCK.

sre-oncall: any logs from the migration job?

eng-release: here's the job tail: 
```
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z migration: applying step 3/6: backfill responses.response_meta
2026-03-15T10:08:22Z migration: waiting for exclusive lock on table responses
2026-03-15T10:10:01Z migration: lock timeout, retrying (attempt 3)
2026-03-15T10:12:30Z migration: stuck, no progress for 8m
```

eng-release: looks like long-running queries (analytics scans) are holding locks. The migration helper should've used non-blocking tactics but it's stuck.

db-ops: jumping in. If alter/add column without default should be fast, but backfill might be updating millions of rows. We need to avoid killing the DB. Can you pause traffic to the codepath that uses the new column?

sre-oncall: initiating feature-flag kill: `ffctl toggle new-metrics-write --off --env prod`

incident-bot: ACTION: feature flag new-metrics-write set to OFF by sre-oncall at 10:16 UTC. Traffic should stop hitting new column. Give it 1m for in-flight to clear.

matt-support: after flag off, 5xx rate dropped from 8% -> 1.3% within 45s. Affected customers still have a handful of errors but overall better.

carla-prodeng: good catch. We still have the migration job stuck and some sessions holding locks. We should coordinate a safe mitigation: graceful cancel of migration backfill, restart migration in smaller batches, or let it finish in maintenance window. We also need to confirm whether any schema mismatch remains on read replicas.

db-ops: I'll inspect pg_stat_activity. Running query: `SELECT pid, usename, state, query_start, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query ILIKE '%ALTER TABLE%' OR query ILIKE '%backfill%';`

db-ops: found one backend: pid=48217, user=deploy_migration, state=active, query_start=2026-03-15 10:05:12, query="UPDATE responses SET response_meta = ...". Also several long-running ANALYZE/SELECTs by analytics user pids 47001-47004. Those are holding read locks but shouldn't block the update; looks like the migration attempted an exclusive lock for a DDL variant and the analyzer holds continuous advisory/pg_class locks.

sre-oncall: we need minimal customer impact. Options: 1) kill migration session (pid 48217) to unblock and rollback; 2) cancel analytics queries (coord with analytics team); 3) temporarily set DB to read-only for non-essential analytics. Thoughts?

eng-release: if we kill migration mid-backfill, the migration helper should detect partial progress and revert schema changes or leave column in NULL state. The code will be gated by ff which we turned off, so safe. I prefer kill migration and then re-run a batched backfill later.

db-ops: agreed. I'll cancel the migration session first: `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(48217);` If it doesn't stop, escalate to `pg_terminate_backend(48217);` after confirming no unsafely long locks.

sre-oncall: proceed. Notify if you need us to scale read replicas or rotate connections.

db-ops: pg_cancel_backend returned true, session is finishing. Observing cleanup logs: `migration: caught cancel, rolling back step 3`. Good. Locks releasing.

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident severity downgraded from P1 -> P2 (major but contained) at 10:24 UTC after flag kill and migration cancel.

matt-support: customer impact update: after mitigation, acme-inc and skyfarm reported temporary errors but restored. Polaris-ml still had some queued writes; support team applied manual retries for ~120 in-flight jobs. We'll follow up with postmortem communication.

carla-prodeng: next steps: 1) keep flag off, 2) mark migration as cancelled and create a batched backfill plan (window: 03/16 02:00-04:00 UTC), 3) add a pre-check to the deploy pipeline to ensure migration progress or safe mode, 4) update runbook to treat backfills as potential lock risks when analytics workload high.

eng-release: I'll patch the deploy pipeline to run `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE relation = 'responses'::regclass` before kicking the backfill job; if locks>0 fail fast. I'll also add a guard to only run backfill with `--max-batch-size=10000`.

sre-oncall: documenting timeline and handing off to db-ops for cleanup. I'll leave the thread open for the on-call rotation. Next oncall, please pick this up: `@db-ops` you have ownership for the next hour; handoff at 11:00 UTC to oncall-night.

db-ops: taking ownership for cleanup and replan. I'll verify replicas and ensure no schema drift. Expected ETA for plan doc: 45m.

matt-support: writing customer advisory draft now, will post to affected accounts and add link to incident ticket.

carla-prodeng: thanks everyone. Add runbook note: if a feature flag gate allows code to hit a schema that is in-progress migration, we should fail deploy or prevent flag rollout until migration successfully completes on all DB pods.

sre-oncall: final note before handoff: incident-bot page resolved for oncall rotation; severity P2, impacted ~5 customers briefly, root cause: backfill held by long-running queries causing migration lock + flag allowed canary traffic. Postmortem ticket created: https://pm.redwood.example/incident/1759456789

incident-bot: Incident created: ID INC-2026-1759456789, state: active -> monitoring. Pager duty: incident acknowledged by sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: handing off to @db-ops. Next update within 30m or sooner if things change.

db-ops: will update thread when the cleanup plan doc is posted and when maintenance window scheduled.

matt-support: posted customer advisory to affected accounts and Slack channel #customer-updates. Closing ticket for support on this thread.

carla-prodeng: adding owners for the postmortem: eng-release (cause/migration code), db-ops (mitigation/replan), prod-support (customer comms), sre-oncall (runbook updates).

sre-oncall: thanks team. Leaving channel for rotation. :thumbsup:
